name: Injera
description: Spongy, slightly sour flatbread made from fermented teff batter. It is the plate, the spoon and the foundation of almost every Ethiopian meal.

name: Doro Wat
description: Slow-cooked chicken stew built on berbere spice, onions and niter kibbeh, usually served with hard-boiled eggs. Considered the national dish and a centerpiece of holidays.

name: Kitfo
description: Finely minced beef seasoned with mitmita and spiced butter, served raw, lightly warmed (leb leb) or cooked. Rooted in Gurage cuisine and often paired with ayib cheese and gomen.

name: Shiro
description: Silky stew of ground chickpea or broad bean flour simmered with onion, garlic and berbere. A fasting-day staple.

name: Tibs
description: Sautéed cubes of beef or lamb with onion, green pepper and rosemary. Served sizzling for celebrations or casual dinners.

name: Gomen
description: Collard greens gently stewed with garlic, ginger and onion. A cooling counterpoint to spicy wats.

name: Misir Wat
description: Red lentils simmered in berbere until thick and deeply flavored. A cornerstone of the vegan fasting platter.

name: Dulet
description: Finely chopped tripe, liver and lean beef pan-fried with onion, chili and spices. A bold, traditional breakfast or celebration dish.

name: Firfir
description: Shredded injera tossed in spiced sauce, with or without meat. A clever way to use up leftover injera.

name: Genfo
description: Thick barley or wheat porridge with a well of spiced butter and berbere in the center. A traditional breakfast and new-mother dish.

name: Ful
description: Mashed fava beans cooked with onion, tomato and spices, often topped with olive oil, egg or yogurt.

name: Tej
description: Honey wine flavored with gesho (buckthorn) leaves. Served in a round-bottomed flask called a berele.

name: Buna
description: Ethiopian coffee, prepared in a clay jebena during the traditional coffee ceremony. Ethiopia is widely regarded as the birthplace of coffee.

name: Kolo
description: Roasted barley, often mixed with peanuts or chickpeas. Served alongside coffee and eaten on journeys.
